A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 29-page versions of the same PVP study. Their main text, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original human persuasiveness ratings, dataset analyses, evaluator and generator experiments, and supplementary validation and error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original human-rating and model experiments and reports revised analyses of associations between psychological characteristics and persuasiveness.

M1.justification: The dataset-construction procedure, evaluator inputs and outputs, image-description generator, and SFT/QLoRA training approach are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 28,454 images, 596 messages, 20 topics, nine strategies, and 2,521 Korean annotators. Evaluator and generator tasks, image sources, and the unseen-message scenario are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and LLaMA3-8B-Instruct with the same zero-shot, fine-tuned, input-format, and psychological-characteristic configurations. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The reported splits, metrics, filtering criteria, training budgets, and unseen-message testing procedure are unchanged. Appendix B.1 retains the same four-bin Spearman-correlation procedure despite the revised coefficients; no protocol change is documented.

E4.justification: The supplementary analyses of which psychological characteristics relate to strategy and topic effectiveness are substantially revised in Figures 5–6, including inverse associations absent from v1. The evaluator ablations, generalization test, and generator error analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain seed 42, generator standard-deviation reporting, and the image-validation procedure using 40 GPT scores, 1,000 bootstrap samples, and 95% confidence intervals. The revised correlations introduce no documented significance tests or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figures 5–6 replace many correlation magnitudes and directions. In Figure 5, negative consequence–agreeableness changes from 0.95 to -0.32, and negative consequence–stimulation changes from 1.00 to -1.00. Topic-association findings also change, while model-performance results in Tables 2–5 and 11–12 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The conceptual definitions and stated correlation methodology are retained. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and v2 introduces no mathematical derivation or revised assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same dataset contribution, two proposed tasks, and claims about the utility of psychological characteristics and fine-tuning. The revised association findings do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 replaces explanations emphasizing social harmony and extraversion with accounts involving pleasure, novelty seeking, moral concern, and conscientiousness, including potentially counterproductive loss framing. Appendix B.2 substantially revises which psychological characteristics explain responsiveness to particular topics. The limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Prompts, preprocessing instructions, QLoRA parameters, learning rates, epochs, hardware, and training times are retained. The reported repository, license, and Google-image URL access information are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to persuasion datasets, psychological frameworks, and image-aesthetics research are unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in Section 4.4 and Appendix B.2, with author-affiliation and contact updates on the first page. The overall narrative, section organization, and appendix structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 5–6 are redrawn with axes accommodating negative correlations and diverging heatmap colors, while retaining their panel structures. Figure 4 moves from page 8 to page 9, with accompanying text and table reflow; no figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 makes inverse associations explicit in Figures 5–6 and aligns its discussion with those revised findings. However, substantial coefficient reversals are unexplained while Appendix B.1 reports the same analysis procedure. With the main experiments and reproducibility information unchanged, the PDFs do not establish whether the revised analysis is more reliable, preventing a confident judgment of overall improvement.
